frontier.hypothesis: The only remaining route inside the measured model is a byte-neutral reference lift: the walk pointer must carry ~9 extra RA-time references (5 -> >=14) that do not materialize as bytes.
frontier.mechanism: jump2's find_cross_jump runs AFTER register allocation, so a REAL statement duplicated into two control-flow arms is counted twice by flow.c's reg_n_refs and then re-merged to identical bytes — the sanctioned [[duplicated-statement-into-arms]] family, whose documented use is exactly a reg_n_refs priority lift for global-RA walls. Every other post-RA pass was checked and creates no new references here.

frontier.hypothesis: If the duplication axis also measures dead, the function's honest state is that no C with these RTL reference counts can produce the target allocation — which is a forensics question about which RA-time reference counts the ORIGINAL C had, not a search question.
frontier.mechanism: The bytes pin 12 buffer accesses through the $s1 holder and 5 through the $s0 walk pointer; allocno_compare then forces the $s1 holder to sort first. Either some references were introduced after global_alloc (only cross-jump/reorg can do that, both checked) or the original's flow-time counts differed for a reason not yet identified.
frontier.next_probe: Forensics modality: instrument/dump the full RTL insn stream at flow, sched and global_alloc for the best form (cc1 -da plus BB2_SCHED_DEBUG/BB2_XJUMP_DEBUG) and enumerate, insn by insn, every target byte whose reference could have been created after RA.
